trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.

Going up would force the two-exit cells to link up into a loop (or put the numbers out of order); going right would force the two-exit cells to link up into a loop (or put the numbers out of order). So the line goes down.
The line must go right: left is number 8, which comes later.
I can't rule out up or right yet, so I'll make an educated guess: up.
Going right, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes left.
Cell (4,3) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes left.
Going up, the next 3 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (5,1); going left, the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (5,1). So the line goes down.
Cell (3,2) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes right.

Contradiction! Every way forward fails: going up leaves no safe move afterwards; going right, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So my guess (up from cell (5,5)) was wrong, so the line must go right.
Going right would leave both cell (4,7) and cell (6,7) needing the line next, and it can't do both; going down would force the line onto number 7 before its turn. So the line goes up.
Going up, the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (3,7). So the line goes left.
The line must go left: up is number 6, which comes later.

Number 4 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going right would force the line onto number 6 before its turn; going up would cut off the top-left corner (6 cells). So the line goes left.
Cell (2,2) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes left.
Going down, the next 2 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (3,6). So the line goes right.
Cell (1,7) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.
Cell (2,6) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes left.
Cell (6,6) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes up.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes left.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
